svg.title: Target architecture
svg.desc: Git is the source of truth. It holds hub-config (ACM, Tekton, cert-manager), the fleet-clusters repository with provision/NAME/ (ClusterDeployment, MachinePool, install-config, tier label), tekton/pipelines (provision, post-provision, deprovision), and workloads/TIER (day-2 manifests). The hub cluster is trusted. Inside it, Tekton is the workflow engine: an EventListener receives the git webhook on commit and triggers the provision and post-provision pipelines by path and the deprovision pipeline on a deletion PR. Git is also read by the provision pipeline during the run, and ArgoCD syncs Git to the hub-config Application, which delivers Tekton, ACM and cert-manager. ArgoCD is used for manifest delivery only. The provision pipeline applies Crossplane CRs for AWS IAM user generation, which produces per-cluster credentials and generates AWS creds for the Hive controller. The provision pipeline applies cluster CRs to Hive and waits for ready. Hive provisions the spoke through the cloud API. The post-provision pipeline, for tiers base, virt, ai and coco, requests a cert on the hub from cert-manager (ClusterIssuer internal-ca) in the hub-only secret authority, derives and pushes the leaf cert and key only to the spoke, applies tier manifests through the spoke kubeconfig, configures the IDP, and labels the spoke bootstrapped=true on the Placement / ManagedCluster in ACM / Hive. The Placement feeds the ACM cluster generator of the ApplicationSet, which delivers day-2 workloads to the spoke. The deprovision pipeline deletes the cluster CRs, waits for the uninstall, and cleans the hub-side artifacts in cert-manager. The spoke is third-party accessible. It holds the leaf cert and key with no CA material, baseline operators by tier (CNV, GPU and OAI, sandboxed containers, base), the IDP config with no hub client secret, and day-2 workloads delivered by the ArgoCD ApplicationSet. Constraints: Tekton, ArgoCD and ACM run on the hub; the spoke is third-party accessible.
svg.text: Git changes trigger Tekton pipelines on the hub; the pipelines drive Crossplane, Hive, cert-manager and the spoke.
Tekton + ArgoCD + ACM run on the hub
waits for Hive to be ready
deletes cluster CRs, waits for uninstall
